about: Top-down battle maps (OpenAI image generation through Codex CLI), each drawn over its fight grid and cut to it; originals in ~/Documents/living-tabletop-world-art/.

maps.prompt:
Generate one image and save it as glass-republic--copper-steps.png in the current directory.

A tabletop battle map, square 1:1, seen straight from above (orthographic top-down), of this place: «Медный спуск» — Каменная улица-лестница от Тихого сада вниз к Медной пристани. Наверху парапет, посередине крытый проход, ниже — угол старого дома и мокрые ступени; у подножия — пристань.

The first reference image is the exact layout of the playable field: a 14 by 12 square grid drawn in the middle of the canvas. Keep the same composition and positions: every dark or black square is a solid obstacle that blocks movement or gives full cover, every mid-grey square is a low obstacle that gives partial cover, every square with diagonal hatching is difficult ground. Choose obstacles that belong to this place (for example crates, pillars, rocks, machinery, furniture, rigging) and draw them exactly on those squares, at the scale of one square each. Plain light squares are open floor or ground the figures walk on. The flat grey area outside the grid is the same place continuing beyond the field: fill it with matching terrain of lesser importance, no key features there.

What this field is, in the campaign's own words (Russian; use it to decide what each kind of square looks like, e.g. hatched squares may be water, rubble, a gap between roofs or a drop, not just rough floor): Медный спуск 14 × 12: столбцы с запада (A) на восток (N), ряд 1 — север. Каменная улица-лестница спускается с запада на восток к Медной пристани; столбец N — нижние ступени у воды. Парапет над каналом D3–G3 — укрытие наполовину. Крытый проход под парапетом: стены I4–K4 и I6–K6 (укрытие наполовину), сам проход I5–K5, Ростислав в J5. Угол старого дома на юго-западе: F9–F11, G10, H10–H12, E11–E12 (укрытие наполовину). Мокрые ступени J7 и G8 — трудная местность. Отряд стоит на востоке, «Тихие» выходят с запада из-за угла.

The second reference image shows how this place looks; match its materials, colours and mood from above.

No grid lines, no people, no creatures, no figures, no text, no letters, no numbers, no labels, no compass, no frame. Even soft light from above so the ground reads clearly under game tokens.

Match one consistent house style: original premium illustrated political-intrigue fantasy for adult audiences only (21+), painterly oil and gouache with restrained ink lines, crisp readable silhouettes and a muted, slightly desaturated finish; Vitrazh, a small city republic whose capital lives behind glass: tall double-paned windows, pale stone arcades and wrought-iron balconies over a wide parade square by a slow canal, a high gallery of signal frames holding large panes of coloured glass, stained-glass light falling in soft coloured patches across stone, parquet and faces, long regimental banners of plain colour fields hanging from poles and railings; palette of smoke grey and slate blue, cold window-glass silver, deep ink black, worn brass and copper, faded banner crimson, bottle green, cobalt blue and milky white glass, with warm candle-gold accents; the quiet tension of polite threats, watchful eyes and closed doors; every person shown is clearly a mature adult. Weapons are only blades, spears, axes and crossbows, kept lowered or sheathed; no firearms, no guns, no gunpowder, no cannons, none exist in this world. Banners and glass panes show only plain colour fields and simple geometric shapes; papers, letters, seals and notices carry only blank or illegible marks. No gore, no blood, no wounds, no corpses, no executions, no torture, no anatomy, no weapons pointed at the viewer. No franchise references, no anime look, no photorealism. No text, no lettering, no numbers, no logos, no watermark, no border.
